senses.sense_definition: A form of Protestant Christianity based on Calvinism.

examples.text: The history of <w>Presbyterianism</w> is deeply rooted in the teachings of John Calvin.
Many early settlers in the region practiced <w>Presbyterianism</w> as their primary faith.

senses.sense_definition: A form of Christian church government characterized by rule by bodies of presbyters or elders.

examples.text: The church adopted a system of <w>Presbyterianism</w> to ensure that local elders shared the decision-making power.
Under this model of <w>Presbyterianism</w>, the congregation is governed by elected representatives rather than a single leader.

senses.sense_definition: The faith, polity, and church government of the Presbyterian churches, which invests presbyters with spiritual authority.

examples.text: The theological framework of <w>Presbyterianism</w> emphasizes the authority of the scriptures and the role of the elders.
Scholars often study <w>Presbyterianism</w> to understand the development of democratic structures within religious institutions.
